subject: AI & Agents
title: Embeddings: Words as Numbers
description: A 60-second lesson on Embeddings: Words as Numbers.

hook.text: To an LLM, the word 'king' is a list of 4,096 numbers. And 'queen' is nearby in that space.

buildup.text: Embeddings convert tokens into high-dimensional vectors that capture meaning.

discovery.text: Similar words cluster together. 'Happy' and 'joyful' are close; 'happy' and 'wrench' are far.

twist.text: King - Man + Woman ≈ Queen. The math of embeddings captures analogies.

climax.text: Every sentence becomes a cloud of points in a space with thousands of dimensions.

quiz.question: What do word embeddings capture?
options: Semantic relationships as positions in high-dimensional space
The exact dictionary definition of each word
The number of letters in each word

details.summary: Embeddings convert words into dense vectors of numbers where similar words end up near each other in mathematical space. This numerical representation lets AI models perform calculations on language and discover relationships between words.
details.whyItMatters: Without embeddings, AI cannot process language mathematically. They are the foundation of every modern language model, enabling search engines, recommendations, and chatbots to understand meaning.
takeaways: Embeddings map words to dense numerical vectors in high-dimensional space
Similar words cluster together, capturing semantic relationships
They are the core input representation for every modern language model

faq.question: How do embeddings capture word meaning?
faq.answer: Words that appear in similar contexts during training are placed near each other in vector space. 'King' is near 'queen' and 'ruler' while far from 'banana' — the model learns meaning from usage patterns.

faq.question: What dimensions do embedding vectors use?
faq.answer: Modern embeddings typically use 768 to 4096 dimensions. Each dimension captures some aspect of meaning, though individual dimensions are not easily interpretable by humans. The richness enables nuanced similarity.
